_comment: Enchantment permit-zone boundaries. FIVE zones, matching USFS and recreation.gov. Each boundary is a MAPPED ESTIMATE from OpenStreetMap, positionally cross-checked against the official USFS raster zone map but not a USFS vector (none found published). Per hard rule 5 and docs/DATA-PLAN.md item 5, the app uses these for 'which zone am I generally in', never for hard boundary-line enforcement. A permit is for a specific zone (Core Enchantment lets you camp in any zone); these polygons let the app say which zone a point falls in, with that precision caveat stated wherever it is shown.

provenance.note: Boundary from OpenStreetMap protected_area relation 7547207 ('Colchuck Permit Area'), pulled 2026-08-21, checked 2026-08-23. Positionally cross-checked against the official USFS Enchantment Permit Area zone map (research/osm-permit-zones/usfs-official-zone-map-2026-08-21.jpg) — same five zones, same relative positions — but NOT diffed against a USFS vector at coordinate precision, because no such vector was found published. Treat this outline as a MAPPED ESTIMATE: good for 'which zone, roughly', not for standing on a boundary line and deciding whether a specific campsite is inside it.

_knownGaps: No USFS vector boundary exists on disk; these are OSM outlines, third-party provenance, cross-checked only visually/positionally against the USFS raster map. Edge deviations of a switchback's worth of metres cannot be ruled out. Zone quotas per night (DATA-PLAN item 8) and exact camping-sub-rules per zone are NOT in this file. The routeKm on each zone is the midpoint pin from waypoints.seed.json, kept for ordering, not a claim that the zone is a point.
